answer: Every claim must pass through the karst kiln: before filing, the filer seals the work in clay, ties an ember-red thread around it and leaves it in the kiln at dusk, fired overnight, opened at dawn. The desk checks within a day: the thread must be ash, the seal unbroken and the work intact, proving a real overnight firing, not a swap. A kiln opened early, a thread still whole or a broken seal means rejection and a lost 250-coin bond, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 real firings plus 250,000 coins. One operator filed forty claims from one kiln load; all forty fell when the log showed a single firing.
